clue.text: Trespasser disturbed dog owner by river

indicators.note: something disturbed has been shaken out of its settled order, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, both words together
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone straying onto private land is upset to meet a dog walker beside a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'dog owner' are followed by R, giving WRONGDOER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespasser commits an offence by entering land unlawfully, so is a kind of offender.

clue.text: But such invertebrates didn't figure in its diet!

definitions.text: But such invertebrates didn't figure in its diet!

blocks.clueFragment: But such invertebrates didn't figure in its diet!
blocks.note: surface reading: some creature never ate these spineless animals
setter's reading: the Diet was the 1521 imperial assembly that tried Luther, held in a German city named after these creatures

explanation.walkthrough: Diet is the assembly, not the menu; the joke is that the creatures the city is named after had no part in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Diet of Worms was held in the Rhineland city of that name, which shares its spelling with the soil creatures.

clue.text: Little-known scientist looking into our energy

indicators.note: looking into something means getting inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: taken as written
a BSc is a Bachelor of Science, a science graduate
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An unknown researcher is investigating our power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: O(BSC)UR, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is not widely known, unfamiliar to most people.

clue.text: Hard work at pit, nosing here?

definitions.note: a cryptic hint at the idiom about keeping one's nose to it

blocks.note: a grind is tedious hard work
the pit of a fruit is its stone

explanation.surface: Miners toil underground, poking their noses about the coal face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit' suggests a coal mine; it is the stone in a cherry. The definition leans on the idiom 'nose to the grindstone', meaning to work hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working relentlessly keeps their nose to the sharpening wheel, so that is where nosing happens.

clue.text: Basket-maker's girl right to take lowest position

indicators.note: the letter for right moves to the bottom of this down entry, the rest staying in order

blocks.note: a girl's name; its first letter R stands for right

explanation.surface: A craftsman's daughter has the right to sit at the bottom of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the lowest position is the end, so R moves from the top of ROSIE to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Osier is willow whose pliant shoots are woven into baskets, the weaver's raw material.

clue.text: Basis of logic later modified around part of Scotland

indicators.note: something modified has been altered, so these letters change their order
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the place

blocks.note: taken as written
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: The foundations of reasoning were later revised in a Scottish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Later' looks like a time word in the surface but is the raw material; the Scottish part is the Hebridean island of St Columba's abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or justification on which an argument rests.

clue.text: Burns briefly displayed by this spiritual leader?

indicators.note: said briefly, the name is cut short and loses its final letter

blocks.note: Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet, is affectionately called Rabbie

explanation.surface: It sounds like a religious figure whose sermons display the poetry of Burns.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns is not about fire: it is the poet. Drop the last letter of his Scots nickname to get RABBI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher, a leader of a congregation in matters of faith.

clue.text: Made into a parcel, say, and carried away

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken aloud, to be heard as another spelling

blocks.note: a parcel is wrapped up in paper

explanation.surface: Something is parcelled up and taken off by the courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried away' looks like the parcel being delivered; it means entranced.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rapt is completely absorbed or enchanted, transported by emotion.

clue.text: Doing well financially, as 26 may be

blocks.note: first meaning: enjoying rapid economic growth
second meaning: 26 across is a marsh bird famous for its deep resonant call

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the bird at 26 across, whose mating call is a deep foghorn-like sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriving economy is described as this, and the bittern's call is a deep hollow resonant noise of the same name.

clue.text: Make sense of name, prettier in translation

indicators.note: translating turns words into something else, so these letters are recast

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A name sounds nicer once translated into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Make sense', with 'of' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to explain the meaning of something, so to work out what it signifies.

clue.text: Batting in Antarctic territory, he scored regularly

indicators.note: the batting word goes in, placed inside the territory's name

blocks.note: Ross Island, written Ross I. on maps, lies in the Ross Dependency of Antarctica
a batsman who is batting is in

explanation.surface: A cricketer playing in Antarctica racks up runs match after match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' looks like cricket after 'Batting', but it means wrote music. The final I is best read as the map abbreviation for Island, as in Ross I.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was a prolific Italian composer who wrote opera scores at great speed.

clue.text: Prizewinning animal going round ring in outer garment

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the best feline at a show would be the top cat
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A champion show animal is paraded in a ring wearing a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: TOP CAT goes round O to give TOPCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A topcoat is an overcoat, worn over the rest of one's clothes.

clue.text: Reliable covering protecting piano suitable for concerts?

definitions.note: a playful definition: a room built for music keeps sound in

indicators.note: protecting something means covering it on all sides, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a sound argument or investment is a reliable one
a roof is the covering of a building
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A trustworthy dust cover keeps a concert grand safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' looks like the instrument under its cover, but it stands for the dynamic marking meaning softly.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundproofed rooms such as recording studios stop noise leaking in or out, useful where music is performed.

clue.text: Mole's equal, by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by the sound tells us to listen for a different spelling of the same spoken word

blocks.note: a peer is an equal, someone of the same rank

explanation.surface: It seems to be about who counts as a mole's equal among animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Mole is not the burrowing animal but a stone breakwater, a sense solvers soon learn to expect.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a massive harbour wall or jetty, which is a kind of pier.

clue.text: Singer in market with son, reversing order completely

indicators.note: the pieces are joined with their sequence turned end to end, last word first

blocks.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
with means together with, plus
a mart is a market
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer at a market stall with his boy turns everything upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'in market with son' are each converted, then strung together in reverse order: S, AND, MART, IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords call any songbird a singer, and the sand martin is a small swallow-like bird.

clue.text: Consort ignoring bishop's warning

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A royal husband pays no heed to a cleric's caution.
explanation.walkthrough: ALBERT without the B leaves ALERT.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a signal telling people of danger, so a noun meaning a caution.

clue.text: Danger Hillary initially encountered in a 17?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the name before it
being encountered in something means being found inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 17 down, a curtain
Edmund Hillary, who first climbed Everest

explanation.surface: It sounds like a peril the mountaineer Hillary faced on a great climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 looks like 17 across, an adventure; it is 17 down. H goes inside A VALANCE, near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sliding down a mountain is a deadly hazard to climbers.

clue.text: Port vessels from East supplied with incense

indicators.note: read from the east, an across word runs right to left, backwards
being supplied with something means having it added on after

blocks.note: vats are large vessels for liquids
to incense is to make furious, as a verb

explanation.surface: Ships arriving from the Orient bring cargoes of incense into harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incense' looks like the perfumed smoke; it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable. STAV + ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Stavanger is a major Norwegian seaport and oil town on the North Sea coast.

clue.text: Wine USA sent out to accommodate a monarch

indicators.note: out here means out of order, so these letters are scrambled
accommodating someone means giving them room inside

blocks.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: America ships wine abroad to put up a visiting king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent out' reads as one phrase; split it, as 'sent' is fodder and 'out' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white dessert wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Opening welcomed by a woodcutter, not entirely speculation

indicators.note: not entirely means falling short of the whole, so the last letter goes
something welcomed by another is taken in, so it sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written
Albrecht Dürer, the German artist, was a master of woodcuts
a vent is an opening for air or gas

explanation.surface: A lumberjack greets a new gap in the forest, half guessing what it means.
explanation.walkthrough: A woodcutter here is not a lumberjack but a maker of woodcuts. A DURE(R) takes in VENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure in its commercial sense is a risky venture, a speculative undertaking.

clue.text: Curtain man installed in centre of Dover church

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter
something installed in a place is put inside it

blocks.note: the middle of five letters
CE is the Church of England
any man's name will do; here Alan

explanation.surface: A man fits a drape in the middle of a church in Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: V + CE take in ALAN: V(ALAN)CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A valance is a short drapery hung along the top of a window or the base of a bed.

clue.text: Bank's implication?

blocks.note: first meaning: a heap of snow or sand piled up by the wind
second meaning: the general sense or gist, as in getting someone's meaning

explanation.surface: It asks what a financial institution is hinting at.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank looks financial; here it is a mound of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowdrift is a bank of snow, and the drift of a remark is its underlying meaning.

clue.text: A Middle-Easterner, I read up I Kings

indicators.note: in a down entry, read upwards means read bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
King Lear is Shakespeare's king, so kings can be Lears

explanation.surface: Someone from the Middle East studies the biblical book of I Kings.
explanation.walkthrough: I Kings is a book of the Bible, which tells of the kings of the land in question; but it splits into I and Kings, read upwards after the opening I.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a citizen of Israel, a Middle Eastern country.

clue.text: Crony small child abandons altogether

indicators.note: abandoning a place means leaving it, so those letters drop out

blocks.note: altogether means completely
a tot is a toddler

explanation.surface: A little one completely walks out on a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: TOTALLY loses TOT, leaving ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A crony is a close companion or supporter, much like a friend on one's side.

clue.text: Plant producing ground-breaking device after others

indicators.note: one thing coming after another sets the second piece behind the first

blocks.note: the rest means the others
a harrow is a farm implement that breaks up soil

explanation.surface: A factory turns out pioneering machines following its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' tempts as a factory and 'ground-breaking' as innovative; both are literal. Restharrow got its name because its tough roots stopped the harrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Restharrow is a pink-flowered wild shrub of the pea family with tough roots.

clue.text: Big cat has change of heart, seeing river

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, and changing it swaps in another

blocks.note: the tiger is the largest big cat

explanation.surface: A tiger relents on spotting a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle G of TIGER becomes B, giving TIBER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the Italian river that flows through Rome.

clue.text: The sort of weather that makes us nervous?

blocks.note: first meaning: blustery, with strong gusts
second meaning: British slang for scared, from having the wind up

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as weather that frightens people; in British slang 'windy' itself means jittery, as in 'to have the wind up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusty weather has this name, and the same adjective is old slang for frightened or jumpy.

clue.text: Garland draped round very short Hebrew patriarch

indicators.note: something draped round another hangs about it, enclosing it

blocks.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
very shortened to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A wreath is hung on a tiny biblical elder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very short' is not a description of the patriarch but an instruction to abbreviate the word very.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was a son of Jacob and founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

clue.text: Is unable even to find somewhere to eat

blocks.note: can't means is unable
e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: Someone cannot even manage to find a place to have lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN'T + E'EN; the apostrophes vanish in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a cafeteria in a workplace, school or barracks where meals are served.

clue.text: Bird injured by dog outside run?

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: what a dog does when it injures someone
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A bird is hurt when a dog catches it out on a run.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTEN goes around R: BIT(R)TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a secretive marsh-dwelling heron with a booming call.

clue.text: In time, learn about fragrant resin

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the following words, sitting within them
turned about means facing the other way, so read right to left

blocks.note: the letters running across the two words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: In due course you'll find out about a sweet-smelling gum.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards through 'tIME LEarn' to find ELEMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic gum from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Group the Italian agent brought round with flexibility

indicators.note: something brought round another is wrapped about it, so it encloses the rest

blocks.note: a ring is a group, as of dealers or spies
il is Italian for the
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A band and an Italian operative are won over by a supple approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' is a gang in the criminal sense, the kind of ring a spy might infiltrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something springily means with bounce and resilience, as an elastic thing behaves.
